AWARD  1.

Brief facts of the present case are that on 02.04.2019 at about 6:30 A.M.
 the deceased went for morning walk at Daulatpur Chowk, Jhatikara Road,
 N Delhi.
When he was crossing the road near Bus Stand of village  Dauladtpur Delhi.
A motor cycle bearing No.UP81R2230 being driven  by R.1 came from the side of Jhatikra in a very high speed in rash and  negligent manner and hit the deceased.
Deceased received injuries.
He has  removed to RTRM Hospital, where he has expired.
2. The investigation was carried out and accordingly the present DAR was  filed before this Tribunal.

It is contending that said accident took place, due MACT no.882/20019 Laxmi Vs Ravi Kumar Page 9 of 18  to rash and negligent driving by Ravi Kumar (respondent no.1/ Driver)
 who was driving motor cycle bearing No.UP81R2230.

sentences.text: The offending  vehicle was owned by ( respondent No.2/ owner) Sh Vinod Kumar and  insured with ( respondent No.3/ Bajaj Allianz General Insurance  Company).

The DAR has been converted into claim petition.
The LRs of the deceased  were made as claimants in the petition.
3. The Respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their W.S.
It is stated that
respondent No/1 driver was at a very slow speed but it was the deceased  who himself negligent and received grievous injuries.
The respondent No.1  is not responsible for the alleged accident.
4. The Respondent no.3 has filed W.S/ legal reply and offered an amount of  Rs.5,00,000/ which was not acceptable to the claimants.
5. After completion of the pleadings, following issues were framed on  05.10.2020 :

(i) Whether deceased Sh Duli Chand sustained fatal injuries in a motor  vehicle accident dated on 02.04.2019 caused due to rash and negligent  driving of vehicle ( Motorcycle) UP81R2230 being driven by R1 Ravi  Kumar, owned by R2 Vinod Kumar and insured with R3 Bajaj Allianz  General Insurance Company Ltd ?

sentences.text: I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioner and Insurance Company.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under:
ISSUE NO. 1: (i) Whether deceased Sh Duli Chand sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 02.04.2019 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle ( Motorcycle) UP81R2230 being driven by R1 Ravi Kumar, owned by R2 Vinod Kumar and insured with R3 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd ? OPP.
9.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this fact petitioners examined PW2 Sh Ravinder Kumar.
He has deposed that on 02.04.2019 at about 6:30 A.M, he was standing at the Bus Stand of Village Daulatpur to board a bus.
He has deposed that a motor cycle bearing No.UP81 R2230 being driven by R.1 came from the side of Jhatikra in a very high speed in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased.
He had made a call at 100 number and also informed the family members of the injured.
PW 1 has been duly crossexamined by all the respondents.
But the testimony of the said PW with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the record only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that deceased was at fault, in any way.
In cross examination of PW 2 ( eye witness) it is proved that the offending vehicle had hit the deceased when he was crossing the road.

sentences.text: The fact that Duli Chand died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.

Moreover,after investigation,
police indicted respondent no.1as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle bearing No. UP81R2330 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh Duli Chand.
So prima facie a fact has been brought on record that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligent.

11. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Sh Duli Chand died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of a motor cycle bearing No. UP81R 2330 by respondent no.1.

ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so,
what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
12.
The Petitioner no.1 is the wife of deceased Sh Duli Chand and petitioner No2 to 10 are children of deceased as such LRs of victim.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
PW1 Smt Laxmi has deposed that her husband was aged about 84 years at the time of accident.
She has deposed her husband was retired from Delhi Administration as a Teacher and was drawing a pension of Rs. 38,325/ p.m.

She has further deposed that deceased had left behind 10 dependents which includes petitioner No.1 and petitioner No.2 to 09 Mact No.882/20019 Laxmi vs Ravi Kumar Page 1 Of 18 on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24135132/
8 as L.Rs of deceased Sh Duli Chand 14.
It is not disputed that deceased was a retired Teacher and drawing a MACT no.882/20019 Laxmi Vs Ravi Kumar Page 12 of 18  pension of Rs. 38,325/ p.m.
So this Tribunal of the considered view that earnings of deceased was Rs.38,325/ per month at relevant time.
15 The age of the deceased was 84 years at the time of accident,
As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court there will be no addition of income of deceased for adding future benefit .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Rather after the death of deceased, who is pensioner, the pension amount for his family will remain 50% ie Rs.19,162.50/
p.m.

Ld Counsel for the petitioners has also fairly admitted that 50% of the pension being drawn at the time of accident will be considered as monthly income of the deceased for computation of compensation.

So I also considered 50% of the last pension of deceased as his monthly income, which comes to Rs.19,162.50/
16.
The deceased was having 10 LRs, it is presumed that deceased was spending 1/5th of his income on his personal expenses.

So the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs. 15,330/ (19,162.50/ 
3832.50/) per month.
17.
To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 05 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.

Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 9,19,800/
(15,330/ x 12 x 05. )
This amount of Rs. 9,19,800/is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

18. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioners no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs.
4,40,000/ (Rs. 44,000/ each to all the petitioners) for loss of consortium,
making a total sum of Rs.13,93,800/

19 . So far as the submission of Ld Counsel for the respondent No.3 that all the claimants are not dependents as they are major and having independent income.

The Submission of Ld Counsel for Respondent No.3, Insurance Company is not acceptable in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in India in case titled National Insurance Co. Ltd Vs Birendere and Ors CA Nos.242 and 243 of 2020, decided on 13.01.2020 and Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana.

The Hon'ble Superior Court in the said judgment has observed that "
even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal Mact No.882/20019 Laxmi vs Ravi Kumar Page 1 Of 18 on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24135132/
9 repesentatives can applied for compensation and observed that the major,married and earnings sons were dependent upon the earnings of the deceased who expired in the accident".
20. Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no. 3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.3 on the date of accident.

Moreover, the evidence of the petitioner fully supports his case, therefore, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against MACT no.882/20019 Laxmi Vs Ravi Kumar Page 14 of 18  respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from  respondent no.3.

My issuewise findings are as under:
ISSUE NO. 1: (i) Whether deceased Sh Duli Chand sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 02.04.2019 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle ( Motorcycle) UP81R2230 being driven by R1 Ravi Kumar, owned by R2 Vinod Kumar and insured with R3 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd ? what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He had made a call at 100 number and also informed the family members of the injured.
PW 1 has been duly crossexamined by all the respondents.
But the testimony of the said PW with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the record only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that deceased was at fault, in any way.
MACT no.882/20019 Laxmi Vs Ravi Kumar Page 11 of 18  10.
The fact that Duli Chand died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
Moreover,after investigation,
police indicted respondent no.1as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.
Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle bearing No. UP81R2330 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh Duli Chand.
So prima facie a fact has been brought on record that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligent.
